headerDisplay: Control an Eliot sit-stand desk with the Smart Dongle from the Home app, over Bluetooth. Requires Linux — the plugin talks to BlueZ.
footerDisplay:
The dongle advertises as **Schreibtisch** and has no vendor name, so it can be hard to spot. Run `node tools/eliot-probe.js scan` on the Homebridge host to find its address.

The desk appears as a window covering: 0% is the lowest height it is set to allow, 100% the highest. Those come from the desk's own limits, so changing them on the handset changes what 0% and 100% mean.

name.title: Name
name.description: Only the log prefix. Each desk is named separately below.

name.title: Name
name.description: What the desk is called in the Home app.

mac.title: Dongle address
mac.description: Bluetooth address of the Smart Dongle.

idlePollSeconds.title: Idle refresh (seconds)
idlePollSeconds.description: How often to ask a standing desk for its height. The desk reports by itself while the control box is driving, so this only catches the handset being used. 0 turns it off. Leave it in seconds, not milliseconds: asking mid-move cancels the move.

memorySwitches.title: Memory switches
memorySwitches.description: Offer the desk's memory positions as switches. They spring back after being pressed, like a scene. Only positions the desk actually has are shown, so an unused memory gets no switch. Rename them in the Home app if "Memory 1" is not what you want.

childLockSwitch.title: Child lock as a switch
childLockSwitch.description: Offer the desk's child lock in the Home app. It is the only setting the control box reports back, so it is the only one that can be shown honestly rather than remembered.

ecoMode.title: Eco mode

oneOf.title: Leave the desk as it is

ecoMode.description:
Eco mode and travel speed, set as a pair. Measured on an Eliot desk: about 22 mm/s with eco on, 42.4 mm/s with it off.

**Takes effect only after the desk is reset.** Run the desk to the bottom and hold the down key until it re-homes. Until then it keeps its old speed, whatever this says.

*Leave the desk as it is* writes nothing. The plugin logs what the desk has stored each time it connects, if you want to know where it stands.
